groups.explanation_vi: Hai nhóm gợi ý: So sánh xu hướng của xe buýt và metro từ 2010 đến 2025. / Xe đạp giảm lúc đầu rồi phục hồi..

paragraphs: The line chart compares daily commuter journeys using three forms of transport in Westbridge from 2010 to 2025.
Overall, metro use grew markedly and became the most popular mode, whereas bus travel fluctuated and finished slightly lower; cycling recovered after an early fall.

In 2010, buses carried around 40,000 daily journeys, more than twice the metro figure of 15,000. Bus use peaked at 45,000 in 2015, before declining to 38,000 by 2025. By contrast, metro journeys climbed steadily to 20,000 in 2015 and then rose more sharply to 50,000 at the end of the period.

Cycling accounted for 25,000 journeys at the outset, ten thousand more than metro travel. This figure dropped to 20,000 in 2015, when it matched the metro total, but subsequently recovered to 23,000 in 2020 and 30,000 in 2025. By the final year, cycling remained less common than bus travel despite its late increase, while the metro had moved ahead of both alternatives.

paragraphs: The bar chart compares annual household waste per person in four towns in 2012 and 2022.
Overall, waste generation fell in three of the four towns, with Southport the only exception. Westhaven produced the most waste in both years, while Northfield was the lowest by 2022.

Westhaven had the highest figure in 2012, at 360 kilograms per person, followed by Eastbank at 320 kilograms. Ten years later, both had reduced their waste output, to 300 and 290 kilograms respectively. The decline in Westhaven was therefore twice as large as the 30-kilogram fall in Eastbank. Despite this decrease, Westhaven still led the four-town ranking in 2022, but by a much smaller margin.

Northfield recorded 280 kilograms per resident in 2012, falling sharply to 215 kilograms in 2022, the lowest level shown. In contrast, Southport rose from 240 to 260 kilograms, becoming the third-highest town by the end of the period despite having the smallest initial figure.

groups.explanation_vi: Hai nhóm gợi ý: Hai thay đổi lớn: sưởi ấm giảm, thiết bị tăng. / Nấu ăn và chiếu sáng đều giảm nhẹ..

paragraphs: The two pie charts illustrate the distribution of household energy consumption by purpose in 2000 and 2020.
Overall, heating lost its dominant position to appliances, whose share almost doubled; cooking and lighting both accounted for slightly smaller proportions in 2020.

In 2000, heating made up half of all household energy use, far exceeding any other category. Its share dropped by 15 percentage points to 35% in 2020. By comparison, appliances increased substantially from 20% to 39%, overtaking heating as the leading source of consumption. Together, these two categories represented 70% of the total in 2000 and 74% two decades later, highlighting their continuing dominance.

Cooking represented one fifth of energy use in 2000 and declined marginally to 18% two decades later. Lighting remained the smallest category throughout, falling from 10% to 8%. Together, cooking and lighting therefore comprised just over a quarter of household energy consumption in the later year.

paragraphs: The table compares daily water consumption in three sectors of Riverton in 2010 and 2020, in millions of litres.
Overall, total water use increased moderately, driven by higher industrial and household consumption, while agriculture remained the largest user despite a decline.

Agriculture consumed 450 million litres per day in 2010, by far the largest amount among the three sectors. However, its use fell to 400 million litres in 2020, a reduction of 50 million litres. Even so, agriculture continued to account for exactly half of the city’s total consumption in the final year. Its original share had been just over three fifths, so its relative contribution declined noticeably.

Industry used 180 million litres per day in 2010 and increased sharply to 260 million litres by 2020. Household consumption also rose, albeit by a smaller amount, from 110 to 140 million litres. Combined, these two rises more than offset agriculture’s decline, taking the citywide total from 740 to 800 million litres daily.

paragraphs: The bar chart compares attendance at the Cedar Museum in 2015 and 2025, and the pie chart shows the purposes of visits in the latter year.
Overall, the museum welcomed substantially more visitors in 2025 than in 2015, and leisure was the main reason for visiting in the final year.

The number of annual visitors rose from 120,000 in 2015 to 180,000 in 2025, an increase of 60,000 people. This represents a rise of one half over the decade. The bar chart does not provide any information on visitors’ purposes in the earlier year.

Among visitors in 2025, leisure accounted for the majority of trips, at 55%. Educational visits represented a further 30%, while the remaining 15% of visitors came for other reasons. Leisure was therefore more common than education and other purposes combined. The distribution is reported for 2025 only, so no changes in visit purposes can be inferred.

paragraphs: The two maps illustrate how the layout of Lakeside Park changed between 2005 and 2025.
Overall, the park became more visitor-oriented, with a café, cycle parking and an additional entrance replacing some older features. The pond and the main southern entrance remained in place.

In 2005, a pond occupied the northwestern corner of the park, while a wooded area stood in the northeast. A broad central lawn was linked to the southern entrance by a path. There was also a parking area in the southwest and a small playground to the southeast.

By 2025, the pond and the southern entrance had been retained. However, the northeastern woodland was replaced by a café, and bicycle racks took the place of the southwestern car park. The playground on the eastern side was enlarged, and an additional gate was created on the eastern boundary, connected to the existing path network. A pavilion was also added within the former central lawn.

paragraphs: The diagram illustrates the eight stages through which harvested olives are turned into bottled olive oil.
Overall, it is a linear process that begins with preparing fresh olives and ends with bottled oil, following successive crushing, mixing, separation and filtering stages.

First, olives are harvested and any leaves are removed from the collected fruit. The olives are then washed before being crushed. This is followed by a mixing stage, during which the crushed fruit is turned into olive paste. These initial operations prepare the material for oil extraction. Each action follows the one before it, and the diagram does not display any alternative route or return loop.

Once the paste has been mixed, the oil is separated from it. The resulting oil then undergoes a filtering stage before proceeding to the final operation, in which it is put into bottles. Consequently, the finished product is bottled olive oil rather than unprocessed olives or paste. Although the illustration shows eight ordered stages, it gives no temperatures, durations or amounts; therefore, none of those details should be added to the description.

paragraphs: The diagram illustrates the steps involved in treating used cooking oil before it is stored.
Overall, the procedure begins with collection and removal of solids, then splits according to whether the oil contains water. Both routes subsequently merge at the drying stage and lead to storage.

Initially, used cooking oil is collected and passed through a screen to remove solid material. The screened oil is then inspected. At this point, the route divides into two branches: oil that is clear is sent directly for filtering, while oil found to contain water is transferred to a settling stage. The diagram therefore shows two different treatments rather than a single uninterrupted sequence for every batch.

After filtering or settling, the two streams converge. The treated oil is then dried before being transferred to storage, which is the final step shown. Although the upper and lower routes use different operations immediately after inspection, both reach the same later stages. No recycling loop, processing time or treatment temperature is specified in the illustration, so these should not be inferred when writing the report.
